commentary_segments.text: All previous transconductors use two (or more) differential pairs to increase the input voltage range. Cross-coupling of the output Drains allows linearization of the total output current, which leads to a constant transconductance over a wider input range. Cross-coupling can also be used in single differential pairs to improve the input range. The first example uses MOSTs M3 as series resistances for the input transistors M1. These MOSTs M3 drive a cross-coupled pair which increases the input voltage range. Another example is given next.
